issues.legal_issue: A uniform market value may be adopted for lands in different villages when their relevant characteristics and development potential are similar and a contemporaneous acquisition of comparable land provides a reliable valuation unit.
material_facts: The acquired lands lay in five villages and were connected by roads; the area was developing and had potential for industrial or urban development.
The Court found little to distinguish the lands in the five villages from one another or from the lands in an adjoining village acquired at about the same time.
The adjoining village’s acquired land covered a substantial area and had been valued uniformly.
No contemporaneous document providing a better basis for determining market value was identified.
The High Court rejected belting and valued the acquired lands uniformly; the Union challenged that approach.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the High Court’s uniform valuation and dismissed the appeals, finding no cogent basis to interfere with its decision to treat the lands as a single unit and use the adjoining village’s acquisition as a comparative unit.
issues.legal_principle: Market value may be assessed using comparable acquired land, taking account of the lands’ location, character and development potential. The Court acknowledged the principle in Union of India v. Ram Phool and Ranvir Singh v. Union of India that the price of a small parcel is not necessarily determinative of the value of a vast tract, but found that principle did not preclude comparison here because the adjoining acquisition covered a substantial area and was comparable. The Court also held that local circumstances and features may justify discarding the belting method.

rule.if: land_acquisition_valuation_appeal and comparable_land_was_acquired_contemporaneously and acquired_areas_had_similar_character_and_development_potential and comparable_land_was_substantial and no_better_contemporaneous_market_evidence_was_shown

predicates.land_acquisition_valuation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the determination of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.comparable_land_was_acquired_contemporan: Land used as a comparator was acquired at about the same time as the land whose value is being determined.
predicates.acquired_areas_had_similar_character_and: The acquired areas had similar relevant characteristics, connectivity, and potential for development.
predicates.comparable_land_was_substantial: The land used as a comparator covered a substantial area rather than being merely a small parcel.
predicates.no_better_contemporaneous_market_evidenc: No more suitable contemporaneous documentary evidence of market value was shown.
predicates.uniform_market_valuation_is_upheld: A uniform market valuation for the acquired land is upheld.

issues.definition: When a valuation appeal involves similar acquired areas and a substantial, contemporaneous comparator, with no better contemporaneous market evidence shown, the uniform market valuation is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Entitlement to the additional compensation component under Section 23(1-A) depends on whether the Collector made the award after the applicable eligibility cutoff.
material_facts: The High Court had allowed the benefit of Section 23(1-A) for certain acquired lands.

The Court clarified that the benefit was confined to lands for which the Collector made the award after the applicable cutoff; it identified the lands in two of the villages as meeting that condition.
issues.conclusion: The benefit under Section 23(1-A) is confined to acquired lands for which the Collector made the award after 30 April 1982.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, applies to land where the Collector made the award after 30 April 1982; the Court reiterated that the benefit was limited accordingly.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by the State.
predicates.collector_award_was_after_eligibility_cu: The Collector made the award after the applicable eligibility cutoff.
predicates.additional_compensation_component_is_ava: The acquired land is eligible for the additional compensation component.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition compensation proceeding, the additional compensation component is available when the Collector made the award after the eligibility cutoff.
